Synopsis:
Australia's Regis Healthcare (REG.AX) shares collapsed 27% after the government's AN-ACC funding rate increase of 2.55% fell short of sector wage inflation and operating cost pressures. The funding gap between government indexation and provider operating costs is expected to persist into 2027. Regis is responding by raising room prices and ancillary service fees. A peripheral mention of Australian CPI exceeding forecasts in July raises the prospect of another RBA rate hike, but this is incidental to the article's core focus on aged care sector funding policy.
